scope: Read-only review of CAP8 SHORT collector; synthetic host tests only, no hardware or production edits. Paused after concrete finding for the independent startup memory investigation.
passedChecks: Firmware runtime TX setter/query emits lowercase short/rel/full and collector compares lowercase correctly.
TX? is added to process-local readonly query schema; advertised ble_snapshot_v1 token is checked before TX mutation.
Original unknown TX and non-CAP8 requested configuration do not issue TX setters; already-short is unchanged.
Setter is not replayed. Lost SHORT setter ACK triggers one restoration attempt because attempted is marked before issuing the write.
Restoration shares original total deadline, and a restoration failure does not overwrite an existing primary error.
Raw SHA is calculated by outer run_benchmark only after subclass run/finally returns, so received restore bytes are included and the saved hash matches them.

normal_FULL_loss_budget_applicable=false and snapshot_acceptance=NOT_EVALUATED prevent this collector itself from asserting ordinary FULL delivery acceptance; an independent BLE observer remains required.

findings.reason: Base run creates copied final fault counters/status and byte/elapsed counters before subclass finally performs additional TX restore reads. Faults during the restore setter wait are already present before the following query establishes its own baseline; they therefore do not fail that readonly query. The subclass reports CAPTURED/QUERY_VERIFIED and outer index COMPLETE despite a new MFAULT present in raw.
findings.actualResult: Synthetic real collector, MFAULT injected before the TX=REL ACK: rawContainsRestoreFault=true, rawShaMatches=true, summary firmware_fault_events=0, status=CAPTURED, index=COMPLETE. Even normal restore has rx_bytes34 below the actual raw length.
findings.recommendation: Record fault/reset baselines before restoration; merge final live transport/byte/fault/reset/elapsed observations after restoration. A new restore-phase fault/reset must be a separate cleanup error with ERROR status and preserve any primary error. Do not claim final CAP safety from a check made before the new fault. Keep total deadline, one-shot setters and raw hash ordering unchanged.
